title: SRE standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives and Runbooks
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary

This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for service-level objectives (SLOs), error budget policy, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbook structure. It is intended for all oncall engineers, service owners, product engineers, and platform teams that contribute to production services.

Scope

- Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated and private control plane endpoints) and critical backend services that affect customer SLOs (routing, auth, billing, and model serving runtime).
- Excludes internal dashboards and non-customer-facing CI test infra (those have separate SLOs listed in eng-infra).

SLO definitions and SLIs

Standard SLOs (applies unless a service-specific ADR exists):

1) Availability (Success Rate)
   - SLI: request_success_rate measured as 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) over 30d rolling window.
   - SLO: 99.95% for Hosted API core endpoints (generate/chat/embeddings).
   - SLO: 99.9% for internal control-plane services.
   - Measurement: traffic-weighted by customer tier.

2) Latency
   - SLI: p95_latency_ms and p99_latency_ms for user-facing requests measured at ingress (edge LB) and at model-serving runtime.
   - SLO: p95_latency_ms <= 250ms, p99_latency_ms <= 800ms for Hosted API (typical gen requests, 0-512 tokens).
   - SLO exceptions: large-sequence or streaming routes must document expected latencies in route config.

3) Correctness/Quality (for generation/embeddings)
   - SLI: model_response_completeness and downstream_e2e_eval_failure_rate measured via automated evals and sampled prompts.
   - SLO: 99% of weekly sampled prompts pass baseline eval thresholds; failing regressions trigger rollbacks.

4) Capacity & Throttling
   - SLI: capacity_margin = (provisioned_capacity - observed_peak) / provisioned_capacity.
   - SLO: maintain >= 15% capacity_margin for Dedicated pools and >= 20% for Hosted pooled capacity during business hours (region-local).

SLI instrumentation requirements

- All services must emit the following metrics with tags: service, cluster, region, route, customer_tier:
  - request_total, request_failed, request_latency_ms (histogram), model_kv_cache_hit, queue_length, gpu_utilization_percent, cpu_utilization_percent.
- Metrics must be exported to central telemetry (Prometheus -> Cortex) and stored with 13 months retention for SLOs.
- Error classification: failed_requests must be classified into: client_error (4xx), transient_server_error (5xx retriable), permanent_server_error (5xx non-retriable), model_error (runtime/model-serving errors).

Error budget policy and burn control

- Error budget calculation: error_budget = (1 - SLO) * evaluation_window (30 days by default).
- Burn rate monitoring: run burn-rate windows at 1h, 6h, 24h. Alerts are triggered when burn_rate > 1.0 (single-window) or > 2.0 sustained (6h).
- Operational responses:
  1. Green (burn_rate < 0.5): normal operations.
  2. Watch (0.5 <= burn_rate < 1.0): SRE notified, deeper triage; consider temporary throttles or routing changes if root cause is known.
  3. Restricted (burn_rate >= 1.0): product/PM informed; escalation required to oncall lead; consider progressive restriction policies (see Routing & Throttling section).
  4. Freeze (customer-impacting regression with > 3% budget consumed in 24h): immediate rollback to last known-good model or route variant; customer-facing communications drafted by CS.

- When error budget is exhausted for a service for the remainder of the evaluation window, new non-critical feature rollouts are paused and capacity is conserved for critical traffic.

Capacity planning and scaling guidance

- Capacity planning review cadence:
  - Quarterly capacity review led by eng-sre + eng-platform + product for services with > 1% of traffic or > $100k/mo cost.
  - Monthly operational check for bursty/seasonal customers.

- Headroom targets:
  - Production pools: maintain 15% reserved GPU headroom for Dedicated and 20% for Hosted.
  - Hot routes (95th percentile traffic contributors): keep 30% headroom during known peak windows.

- Autoscaling & policy defaults:
  - Horizontal autoscaling targets are based on request queue length and p95 latency. Default HPA: scale up when queue_length_per_replica > 50 or p95_latency > 200ms for 3m.
  - Vertical scaling for inference pods is controlled via capacity profiles: small/medium/large based on sequence length distribution.

- Cost-performance tradeoffs and optimizer guidance (Redwood Optimize integration):
  - Use batching and prefix KV cache to reduce per-token cost; recommended batch_size defaults: 8 for small models, 16 for medium models, 32+ for large models (adjust by latency SLO).
  - Quantization profiles: reference quantization-profiles page for model-specific guidance and validated accuracy regressions.

Reliability initiatives and continuous improvement

- Quarterly reliability themes (RITs): each quarter choose 1-2 high-impact projects (examples: KV cache eviction tuning, cross-region failover automation, model rollback automation).
- OKR alignment: reliability initiatives must include a measurable metric (SLO improvement, cost-per-token reduction, MTTR reduction).
- Post-implementation monitoring: run 8-week stabilization with additional dashboards and a targeted sample eval set to detect quality regressions.

Incident review standards (postmortem/playbook)

- Every Sev2+ incident requires a post-incident review within 7 business days. The review must include:
  - Summary: timeline, impact (customer-visible metrics), root cause, mitigations, follow-ups, owner for each follow-up.
  - Severity classification and justification.
  - Quantified impact: number of affected requests, error-rate delta, customer list if any.
  - Timeline table with timestamps, actions, and owners.
  - RCA narrative and evidence (logs, telemetry graphs, traces).
  - Corrective actions: short-term mitigations, medium-term fixes, long-term preventative measures with target dates.

- Postmortem template (minimum fields)
  1. Title and incident ID
  2. Date/time window and duration
  3. Services/components impacted
  4. Impact and customer list
  5. Root cause analysis (what, why, how detected)
  6. Timeline (detailed)
  7. Action items (owner + by-date)
  8. Learnings and follow-ups

- Review process: the postmortem must be reviewed in the SRE weekly review meeting; owners for follow-ups tracked in the reliability initiatives board.

Operational tooling and runbooks

- Central tooling:
  - Telemetry: Prometheus/Cortex + Grafana for dashboards; long-term metrics in BigQuery for trend analysis.
  - Tracing: OpenTelemetry -> Jaeger, with traces tied to request_id.
  - Incident comms: Slack #incidents with playbook bot integration for runbook checklists.
  - Oncall routing: PagerDuty with escalation policies defined per service.

- Runbook structure (template)
  - Title, Service, Oncall role (primary/secondary), PagerDuty escalation policy ID
  - Symptoms (how issue appears in dashboards/alerts)
  - Initial triage checklist (commands, dashboards, quick queries)
  - Mitigation steps (ordered, with estimated time-to-mitigate)
  - Recovery validation (metrics to check and expected values)
  - Post-incident steps and owner for postmortem

- Example runbook excerpt (Model-serving OOM/Model-load failures)
  1. Symptoms:
     - high model_error_rate, OOM events on inference nodes, GPU memory pressure > 90%
  2. Initial triage:
     - check recent deploys: kubectl get deploy -n model-serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
     - check GPU memory: runcmd gpu-metrics --cluster $CLUSTER --since 15m
     - check logs for model-loader exceptions: kubectl logs -l app=model-loader -n model-serving --tail 200
  3. Mitigations (ordered):
     a. Scale down new model replicas: kubectl scale deploy/model-<id> --replicas=0
     b. Rollback to previously pinned model revision: run /infra/scripts/rollback_model.sh --service model-<service> --rev <last-good>
     c. If rollback not possible, drain affected nodes and restart runtime: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  4. Recovery validation:
     - model_error_rate < 0.1% across sampled routes
     - p95 latency returns below SLO within 10m of mitigation
  5. Post-incident:
     - open postmortem and assign owner for follow-ups

Ownership, escalation and exceptions

- Service owners must be listed in the service catalog and are responsible for defining service-specific SLOs when default SLOs are insufficient.
- Any deviation from standard SLOs or capacity headroom requires an ADR and approval from eng-sre and product.
- Critical escalations: PagerDuty escalation to SRE oncall -> oncall lead -> engineering director.

Compliance and auditability

- All SLO calculations, burn-rate alerts, and incident postmortems must be retained for a minimum of 13 months for audit and compliance reasons.
- SLO changes and ADRs must be tracked in the architecture-and-standards space and linked from the service catalog entry.

Appendices

A. Alert thresholds (examples)
| Alert name | Metric | Trigger | Severity | Owner |
|------------|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| SLO-burn-1h | error_budget_burn_rate_1h | > 1.0 | P1 | service-oncall |
| p99-latency-exceed | p99_latency_ms | > 800ms for 5m | P2 | service-oncall |
| gpu-saturation | gpu_utilization_percent | > 95% for 10m | P1 | infra-oncall |

B. Useful queries (PromQL examples)
- request_success_rate: 1 - (sum(rate(request_failed[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(request_total[5m])) by (service))
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))

C. References
- eng-sre/sre-slos-capacity-and-runbooks-2026-03-04
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails

If you are the service owner and need help implementing any of the instrumentation, SLO dashboards or a runbook, reach out to eng-sre@redwood-inference.internal (SRE oncall) or open a ticket in the reliability initiatives board.
